CPI(M) state secretary M.V. Govindan on Sunday (November 8, 2026) expressed solidarity with the ongoing agitation by students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit at Kalady near Kochi, saying the protest should continue until all the suspended students are allowed to appear for their examinations.
Also read | Kerala HC ruling on political activities in campuses, Ambedkar and the right to protest | Explained
Sixteen students were suspended after a Students’ Federation of India (SFI)-led protest during a syndicate meeting on August 13 over a lack of adequate campus facilities.
They were accused of staging a “mock cremation” of Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas, manhandling her and attempting to damage university property.
A single bench of the Kerala High Court had directed the university to allow the students to appear for the examinations, but a division bench later stayed the order . The students then approached the Supreme Court, which directed the single bench to decide the matter.
The university said the suspension of 10 of the 16 students would be revoked if they apologised , but they refused.
In a Facebook post after visiting the protest tent and interacting with the students, Mr. Govindan said the agitation would not be called off merely with an apology.
“Everyone knows who has a history of apologising. The students’ agitation will end only after all the expelled students have written their examinations,” he said.
He alleged that the university’s functioning had been disrupted because the Vice-Chancellor rarely visited the institution. Thomas had raised no complaint while the students were protesting, he said, but later filed a police case, in which the students secured bail.
Mr. Govindan alleged that the Governor’s subsequent intervention had aggravated the situation and claimed that the developments were part of a planned RSS agenda.
Accusing the BJP and Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan of working towards the saffronisation of Keralam, he alleged that the two had supported each other during the Assembly elections as well.
Describing student agitations as engines of social transformation, he said society would stand in solidarity with the students’ protest.
